# Security

TSDuck is developed with security in mind. However, if you believe you have found a security vulnerability in TSDuck, please report it as described below.

## Reporting Security Issues

**Please do not report security vulnerabilities through public GitHub issues.**

Instead, please send an e-mail to contact@tsduck.io.

Please include the requested information listed below (as much as you can provide):

- Type of issue (e.g. buffer overflow, etc.)
- Methods and tools which were used in the discovery (including AI tools, if any).
- Location of the affected source code (tag/branch/commit or direct URL).
- Step-by-step instructions to reproduce the issue.
- Proof-of-concept or exploit code.
- Impact of the issue, including how an attacker might exploit the issue.

## Usage of AI

AI has proven to be quite efficient in the detection of security vulnerabilities. Therefore, vulnerabilities which were found with the help of AI tools are welcome, **as long as the process was supervised and verified by a human**.

Specifically, automatic reports from AI without proper proof-of-concept, or demonstrator, or evidence of human validation, will be rejected without further analysis.

## Bug bounty

TSDuck is an unfunded open-source project. Therefore, no bug bounty can be offered.
